chapters.text: Say you are choosing a bag you can trust. A few questions come up again and again, and each one has a straight answer.
Question one: can a zip really lock? Yes. The Hobo 2.0 has lockable zippers, so nobody can open it in a crowd.
Question two: what about the strap? It is cut-resistant, so it is built to stay on your shoulder.
Question three: does RFID matter? The lining blocks card scanners, so your cards stay private while you are out and about.
Next question: where does everything else go? Hidden pockets and smart compartments give each thing a place, so you stop digging.
Last question: what about a table? A strap loops around your chair, so your bag stays right where you left it.
So the answer to all of them is the same bag: lockable zippers, a cut-resistant strap, an RFID lining, hidden pockets and a table strap.

chapters.text: Time to pack the Hobo 2.0 for a weekend away. Watch where each thing goes, and which part of the bag takes care of it.
One: the things you reach for most. Phone, keys, tickets. Hidden pockets keep them easy to find, so you stop digging through the bag.

Next: the walk to the hotel. The cut-resistant strap sits on your shoulder and leaves your hands free for the luggage.
Last: the café stop. Loop the table strap around your chair, and the bag stays right where you left it while you relax.
